_source.description: Major global metallurgical-grade silicon and ferrosilicon production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Silicon chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); Elkem ASA Annual Report 2023 (elkem.com); Ferroglobe PLC Annual Report 2023 (ferroglobe.com); RUSAL Annual Report 2023 (rusal.ru); Hemlock Semiconductor corporate disclosures; Globe Specialty Metals SEC filings; Wacker Chemie Annual Report 2023 (wacker.com); Dow Inc. corporate disclosures; REC Silicon ASA Annual Report 2023 (recsilicon.com); RIMA Industrial corporate reports; China National Bureau of Statistics silicon metal output data; International Energy Agency Critical Minerals review 2024
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary; IEA: CC-BY-4.0
_source.notes: Metallurgical-grade silicon (MG-Si) and ferrosilicon smelter/plant locations. China dominates with ~70% of world production but individual plant-level data is limited; major provincial clusters are represented. Coordinates from company filings, satellite imagery, and USGS MRDS. Capacity figures represent silicon metal content equivalent where available.

_coverage.global_production_unit: silicon metal content (silicon metal + ferrosilicon Si content)
_coverage.known_gaps: China has hundreds of small ferrosilicon furnaces across Yunnan, Xinjiang, Sichuan, Inner Mongolia, and Guizhou that are not individually mapped; only the largest clusters and named facilities are included. Indian ferrosilicon producers are fragmented across many small operations. CIS countries (Kazakhstan, Ukraine) have additional capacity not captured here.

sites.name: Yunnan Yongchang Silicon
sites.notes: One of China's largest silicon metal producers. Yunnan province accounts for ~30% of China's silicon metal output due to cheap hydropower.

sites.name: Xinjiang Hoshine Silicon (Shanshan)
sites.notes: World's largest silicon metal producer. Hoshine's total capacity ~800,000 tpa across Xinjiang sites. Subject to US WRO (Withhold Release Order) since 2021 over forced-labor concerns.

sites.name: Xinjiang East Hope Silicon (Zhundong)
sites.notes: Integrated MG-Si to polysilicon complex in Xinjiang. East Hope is a major vertically integrated silicon/polysilicon producer.

sites.name: Sichuan Leshan Silicon Complex
sites.notes: Major silicon smelting cluster in Sichuan province leveraging hydroelectric power from the Min and Dadu rivers.

sites.name: Gansu Yongdeng Ferrosilicon
sites.notes: Gansu province is a major ferrosilicon production base. Yongdeng county has a dense cluster of ferrosilicon furnaces using cheap coal-fired electricity.

sites.name: Inner Mongolia Erdos Ferrosilicon
sites.notes: Inner Mongolia is China's largest ferrosilicon-producing region. Erdos (Ordos) basin benefits from low-cost coal power.

sites.name: Hunan Chenzhou Silicon
sites.notes: Hunan province silicon metal producer in southern China.

sites.name: Guizhou Ferrosilicon Complex
sites.notes: Guizhou province ferrosilicon and silicon metal cluster. Benefits from hydropower resources in China's southwest.

sites.name: Bratsk Smelter (RUSAL)
sites.notes: Silicon metal smelter co-located with RUSAL's Bratsk aluminium smelter. Uses cheap hydropower from the Bratsk Dam on the Angara River.

sites.name: Shelekhov Smelter (RUSAL)
sites.notes: Silicon metal plant near Irkutsk, Siberia. Part of RUSAL's silicon division.

sites.name: Karemsha Ferrosilicon (Chelyabinsk)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest ferrosilicon producers. ChEMK is Russia's dominant ferroalloy company.

sites.name: RIMA Industrial (Belo Horizonte)
sites.notes: Brazil's largest silicon metal producer. Multiple smelter sites in Minas Gerais state. Uses charcoal from eucalyptus plantations as reductant.

sites.name: Ligas de Aluminio (Breu Branco)
sites.notes: Silicon metal smelter in Para state using hydropower from Tucurui Dam. Supplies Dow's silicones division.

sites.name: Elkem Salten
sites.ownership: Elkem (listed: ELK.OL, majority China National Bluestar)
sites.notes: Elkem's largest silicon metal plant. Located above the Arctic Circle in Nordland county. Uses Norwegian hydropower.

sites.name: Elkem Thamshavn
sites.notes: Historic Elkem smelter in Sor-Trondelag. Operates since 1920s. Produces both silicon metal and ferrosilicon.

sites.name: Elkem Bremanger
sites.notes: Ferrosilicon and specialty alloy plant on Norway's west coast. One of Elkem's oldest facilities.

sites.name: Ferroglobe Chateau-Feuillet (Montricher)
sites.notes: Ferropem silicon smelter in Savoie, France. Ferroglobe (formerly FerroAtlantica + Globe Specialty Metals) is the world's largest western silicon producer.

sites.name: Ferroglobe Anglefort
sites.notes: Ferropem smelter in Ain department near the Rhone. One of several Ferroglobe facilities in the French Alps region.

sites.name: Ferroglobe Sabero (Spain)
sites.notes: Ferroglobe silicon smelter in Leon province, Spain.

sites.name: Globe Specialty Metals (Niagara Falls)
sites.notes: Silicon smelter in Niagara Falls, NY. One of two remaining US silicon metal plants. Uses cheap hydropower.

sites.name: Globe Specialty Metals (Beverly, OH)
sites.notes: Ferroglobe silicon smelter in Ohio. Combined silicon metal and ferrosilicon production.

sites.name: Mississippi Silicon (Burnsville, MS)
sites.notes: One of the newest silicon smelters in the USA, built in 2014. Designed with modern environmental controls.

sites.name: Hemlock Semiconductor (Hemlock, MI)
sites.ownership: Hemlock Semiconductor (Dow Inc. majority, Shin-Etsu minority)
sites.notes: World's largest hyper-pure polysilicon facility for semiconductor and solar applications. Uses Siemens CVD process. Consumes MG-Si as feedstock.

sites.name: Wacker Chemie (Burghausen)
sites.notes: Wacker's main polysilicon production site. One of the world's top 3 polysilicon producers. Also major silicones manufacturer.

sites.name: Elkem Iceland (Grundartangi)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest ferrosilicon smelters. Uses Iceland's cheap geothermal and hydroelectric power.

sites.name: United Silicon (Helguvik, Iceland)
sites.notes: Silicon smelter commissioned 2017, suspended after environmental issues. Designed to exploit cheap Icelandic power.

sites.name: Samancor Ferrosilicon (Meyerton)
sites.notes: Major South African ferroalloy producer at Meyerton, south of Johannesburg. One of Africa's largest ferrosilicon plants.

sites.name: Transalloys (eMalahleni)
sites.notes: Ferroalloy smelter in Mpumalanga province. Produces ferrosilicon and silicomanganese for steelmaking.

sites.name: Minasligas (Ouro Preto)
sites.notes: Ferroalloy producer in Minas Gerais, Brazil. Uses charcoal reductant.

sites.name: Fiven (Lillesand)
sites.notes: Former Saint-Gobain silicon carbide plant. Fiven is world's leading silicon carbide producer. Lillesand plant uses Norwegian hydropower.

sites.name: OFZ Istebne (Slovakia)
sites.notes: One of Europe's largest ferrosilicon producers. Located in northern Slovakia.

sites.name: Erdenet Ferrosilicon (Mongolia)
sites.notes: Mongolian state ferrosilicon producer near the Erdenet copper complex.

sites.name: Subansiri Ferro Alloys (Assam, India)
sites.notes: India produces ~300,000 tpa ferrosilicon across many small and mid-size operations. Major clusters in Assam, Odisha, Meghalaya, and Jharkhand.
